feas.roofs_vs_space: {roof_m2} m² of cool roof needed; about {capacity_m2} m² of roof looks usable.
feas.max_cooling: With the space available, about {max_c} °C is realistic within {years} years.
feas.spots_unknown: We could not load planting spots, so space was not checked.

why.plant_tree: {trees} shade trees give the biggest long-term cooling.
why.cool_roof: {roof_m2} m² of white or reflective roof cools the block in the first summer.
why.shade_structure: {shade} shade sails or canopies over the hottest lanes and stops.
why.awareness: Talk to neighbours, schools and shops so more people join and care for the trees.

map.title: Map the open spots
map.detail: Walk the zone and note roadsides, school yards, mosque and temple grounds, and vacant plots without shade.

plant.title: Plant about {trees} shade trees
plant.detail: Choose wide-canopy species from the list below. Planting at the start of the monsoon gives the best survival.

roofs.title: Coat about {roof_m2} m² of roof
roofs.detail: Lime wash or reflective paint on tin and concrete roofs: a quick win before the hot season.

team.title: Build a team
team.detail: Invite neighbours, your school or office. Every verified action counts toward the shared goal.

care.title: Care for 2 years
care.detail: Water saplings in dry spells and post a photo every 15 days, so you can see each tree's state.

long_term.title: Watch the long-term cooling
long_term.detail: Trees reach full cooling around year 8; the projection shows the line with and without your plan.

next.roof: Coat the first {m2} m² of roof
next.awareness: Hold a short talk with your neighbours

care.year1: Year 1: water twice a week and keep a guard around each sapling.
care.dry: It is the dry season now: water deeply in the early morning.
care.monsoon: It is the rainy season: check drainage and stakes after storms.
care.checkin: Post a photo of each tree every 15 days; Atmos X reminds you.
care.year2: Year 2: water only in dry spells and prune low branches.

air.enjoy_outdoors: Air is clean: a good time to be outside.
air.ventilate: Open the windows to air out your home.
air.sensitive_watch: Very sensitive people should watch for coughing or shortness of breath.
air.ventilate_off_peak: Air out your home in the early morning or late evening.
air.sensitive_reduce: Children, older people and anyone with asthma or heart disease should cut long or hard outdoor activity.
air.windows_peak: Keep windows closed during rush hours.
air.mask_sensitive: Sensitive people should wear a well-fitted N95 or KN95 mask outside.
air.reduce_outdoor: Everyone should cut long or hard outdoor activity.
air.mask_n95: Wear a well-fitted N95 or KN95 mask outside.
air.avoid_outdoor: Avoid outdoor exercise; move activities indoors.
air.purifier: Run an air purifier or fan with a filter if you have one.
air.stay_indoors: Stay indoors as much as possible; seek medical help if you feel unwell.

haor_flood.title: Haor flash flood risk
haor_flood.body: Up to {local_mm} mm locally and {up_mm} mm upstream in Meghalaya over 3 days. Hill water can enter the haor within 24–48 h.
haor_flood.a1: Harvest Boro immediately if 80% of grains are mature.
haor_flood.a2: Move harvested paddy, seed and livestock to high ground.
haor_flood.a3: Check embankments (bãdh) with your neighbours and report breaches to the Upazila office.

rice_heat.title: Heat stress at flowering
rice_heat.body: {days} day(s) at or above 35 °C from {day} (peak {peak} °C). Pollen dies above 35 °C, causing empty grains (chita).
rice_heat.a1: Keep 5–7 cm of standing water in the field during flowering.
rice_heat.a2: Irrigate in the afternoon to cool the canopy.
rice_heat.a3: Avoid spraying pesticides between 10 am and 2 pm.

drought.title: Dry spell / drought risk
drought.body: Only {rain30} mm of rain in the past 30 days (NASA POWER) and {rain7} mm forecast this week, while crops lose ~{et7} mm to evaporation.
drought.a1: Use alternate wetting and drying (AWD) to stretch irrigation water.
drought.a2: Mulch vegetable beds with straw to keep moisture.
drought.a3: Plan supplementary irrigation for transplanted Aman if rain stays low.
drought.body_smap: Soil in the root zone is only {wet_pct}% wet (NASA SMAP; a rule of thumb) and {rain7} mm of rain is forecast this week.

storm.title: Storm / nor’wester risk
storm.body: Wind gusts up to {gust} km/h expected from {day}.
storm.a1_harvest: Harvest mature crops before the storm arrives.
storm.a1_stake: Stake banana, papaya and tall vegetables.
storm.a2: Store seed and harvested grain in sealed bags on raised platforms.
storm.a3: Follow BMD signals and move to a cyclone shelter if told to evacuate.

cold.a1: Cover Boro seedbeds with clear polythene at night, open during the day.
cold.a2: Keep 2–3 cm water in seedbeds and drain cold water in the morning.
cold.a3: Protect livestock with jute sacks and dry bedding.

late_blight.title: Late blight weather
late_blight.body: Cool, foggy and humid conditions for {days} days: ideal for late blight (Phytophthora) on potato and tomato.
late_blight.a1: Ask your local agriculture officer (DAE) which preventive fungicide to use and how much.
late_blight.a3: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately.

monsoon.title: Monsoon onset likely
monsoon.body: Three or more consecutive rainy days expected around {day}.
monsoon.a1: Prepare Aman seedbeds on raised land.
monsoon.a3: Good time to plant trees: survival is highest now.

lightning.title: Lightning risk
lightning.body: Atmosphere is highly unstable (CAPE up to {cape} J/kg) with thunderstorms likely from {day} {time}.
lightning.a1: Leave open fields when dark clouds gather, usually in the afternoon.
lightning.a2: Do not shelter under isolated trees; crouch low with feet together if caught outside.
lightning.a3: Avoid ponds, canals and metal tools during storms.

worker_heat.title: Dangerous heat for field work
worker_heat.a1: Work early morning and late afternoon.
worker_heat.a2: Drink water with ORS every 20 minutes.
worker_heat.a3: Rest in shade; watch for dizziness and stop work if unwell.

heavy_rain.body: Up to {mm} mm of rain in a day from {day} (BMD: 44 mm or more is heavy).
heavy_rain.body_observed: {mm} mm fell in one day recently, {mm72} mm over 3 days (NASA IMERG).
heavy_rain.a1: Open field drains and clear channels before the rain.
heavy_rain.a2: Harvest ripe crops early and move them to a dry place.
heavy_rain.a3: Cover seedbeds and fertiliser stores; delay spraying.

answer.help: I can explain why your area is hot, the weather now and ahead, air quality, farm alerts, your trees, goal and points, nurseries and species, and where the data comes from.
answer.unknown: I can’t answer that from Atmos X data. Try one of these questions.
answer.safety_medical: I can’t give medical advice. If someone feels unwell in the heat, move them to shade, give water and call a doctor or your local emergency number.
answer.safety_medical_heat: Confusion, fainting or very hot, dry skin need urgent care.
answer.safety_chemicals: I don’t give pesticide, fungicide or fertiliser doses. Ask your local agriculture office (DAE in Bangladesh) and follow the label.

tree.1: Water twice a week for the first 12 months, then only in dry spells.
tree.2: Street trees need a guard against goats, bikes and rickshaws.
tree.3: Plant in the monsoon, June to September.
tree.4: Keep 3 m from walls, drains and pipes.

krish.1: Water twice a week for the first 12 months, then only in dry spells.
krish.2: Street trees need a guard against goats, bikes and rickshaws.
krish.3: Plant in the monsoon, June to September.
krish.4: Shallow roots: keep 4 m from walls, drains and paving.

climber.1: Water every other day for the first 3 months, then twice a week.
climber.2: Give it a trellis or wire mesh 10 cm off the wall.
climber.3: Plant in the monsoon, June to September.
climber.4: Trim after flowering to keep it off gutters and wires.

intl.check_nursery: Commonly planted in cities with this climate. Check with a local nursery what grows well and is not invasive where you live.

season.local: Ask a local nursery for the best season

tip.replant: This tree didn’t make it. Replant in the same spot with a hardy species and a guard.
tip.stressed: Leaves look stressed: water deeply at the base in the morning and check again in 3 days.
tip.water_dry: Only {rain_mm} mm of rain in the last week: water 10–15 litres every 2–3 days.
tip.drainage: {rain_mm} mm of rain this week: make sure water drains away from the base.
tip.guard: Keep the tree guard on for the first year so goats and people don’t damage it.
tip.thirsty: This species needs a lot of water while young.
tip.monsoon: Monsoon: no need to water, but clear weeds around the base.
tip.keep_going: Looking good. Keep checking in every 15 days.
